card.occupation: Sales assistant on the flooring and tiles section of a large DIY and home improvement store on a retail park in Taunton. Full-time, around 39 hours a week, including alternate Saturdays and some Sundays.
card.education_detail: Left a Bridgwater comprehensive at 16 in 1995 with a handful of GCSEs, the best a C in maths and design and technology. Went straight into the yard at a local builders' merchant and later did an NVQ Level 2 in Customer Service through work. He also has in-store forklift and manual handling certificates. Never fancied college and doesn't regret it much.
card.household: Lives with his wife Donna (44), a care assistant at a residential home, in a three-bed ex-council semi they bought under right to buy about twelve years ago. Their daughter Kayleigh (20) still lives at home and works at a nail salon in town. Their son Jordan (23) moved to Bristol with his girlfriend last year. There is an elderly Jack Russell called Pickle.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Bridgwater. His dad worked at the old cellophane factory and his mum did school dinners. Church of England by upbringing. He was married in St Mary's and both kids were christened there. Nowadays it's Christmas, Easter and funerals. He'd still call himself a Christian and says a quiet prayer when things are bad, but doesn't make a thing of it. Bridgwater Carnival is a big part of local identity for him: his uncle was in a carnival club and Darren helped build carts as a teenager.
card.professional_persona: The bloke on the floor customers actually want to find. He's chatty, patient with people who don't know what they're after, and honest enough to tell them they don't need the dearer adhesive. He's good at calming down an angry customer and covers shifts when asked. Paperwork, stock counts and remembering to log things on the handheld are not his strong suit, and his supervisor has had words about it more than once. He has no interest in managing anyone.
card.sports_persona: Plays in a Wednesday night pub skittles league and has done for nearly twenty years. It's more about the pint and the banter than the score. He follows Somerset cricket loosely and gets to the County Ground once or twice a summer for a T20. He watches the rugby internationals in the pub. He used to play Sunday league football until his knees went.
card.arts_persona: Not much of an arts person. Carnival is the closest he gets, and he goes every November without fail. He likes 80s and 90s music, has seen Madness and UB40 live, and listens to Greatest Hits Radio in the car. TV is quiz shows, Gogglebox, Traffic Cops and the odd Netflix crime series Donna puts on. He rarely reads a book.
card.travel_persona: Creature of habit. The family have gone to the same caravan park in Cornwall most summers, and he and Donna did Tenerife twice for big anniversaries. He hated the queues at Bristol Airport and didn't care much for the food. He'd happily never go further than Benidorm.
card.culinary_persona: Meat-and-two-veg man who'll call the evening meal tea or dinner without thinking about it. Donna cooks in the week and he does the Sunday roast or a barbecue when the weather's right. Friday is chippy night. He likes a proper pasty, a cheddar ploughman's and a cider, though he's been told to cut back for his blood pressure. He won't touch anything too spicy.
hobbies_and_interests: Wednesday skittles league at the local pub
Bridgwater Carnival, and helping a mate's club with their cart in the autumn
walking Pickle along the river Parrett
pub quizzes, though he's mainly there for the sport and music rounds
pottering in his shed, which he never quite tidies
watching cricket and rugby on telly
skills: decent practical DIY: tiling, laying laminate, basic plumbing
knowing a fair bit about floor tiles, grout and adhesives
keeping a team cheerful on a dull shift
card.career_goals: Doesn't really have any beyond staying put, keeping his hours and getting a bit more each year. He's been asked about team leader and said no thanks, because he'd rather be on the floor than doing rotas. He'd like to pay off the mortgage before he's 60 and maybe do a few hours less once his knees get worse.
card.voice: Friendly, warm and a bit loud, with an easy pace that speeds up when he's telling a story. Light Somerset accent with a soft rolled 'r' and the odd 'alright?' or 'where's that to?', but nothing broad. He says 'er' while he thinks and leans on tags like 'you know' and 'yeah'. He says 'sort of' a fair bit and calls people 'mate' or, now and then, 'my lover' with older women customers. He laughs at his own jokes and picks up the other person's words when he agrees. Silence makes him a bit uneasy, so he fills it with a joke or an anecdote. If he misses a question he'll say 'sorry, say that again?' without embarrassment.
card.typing: Quick and casual on his phone. Mostly lower case, with capitals only where autocorrect puts them. Punctuation is light: a few commas, often no full stop, and sometimes 'lol' or a 'haha'. Apostrophes come and go ('dont', 'its'). Short answers like 'yeah fine thanks' or 'not really, maybe once a year'. He doesn't go back to fix typos.
card.with_strangers: Opens up straight away. He's chatty, jokey and keen to make the other person comfortable, and he'll ask you questions back. Comes across as genuine and a bit self-deprecating, with no airs, and doesn't try to impress. He agrees easily and avoids anything confrontational. If asked an opinion question he'll often say 'I can see both sides, to be fair'. He may wander off topic and need steering back.
small_things: the skittles team being bottom of the league again
the traffic on the M5 by junction 24
a customer who wanted to tile a bathroom in an afternoon
Somerset doing well or badly in the T20
carnival night and how many people turned up
the price of a pint going up at his local
deeper_things: his dad dying of a heart attack at 61, which is part of why his own blood pressure worries him more than he lets on
a stretch about eight years ago when he was laid off from the builders' merchant and they were skint for months
missing his son since he moved to Bristol, and feeling the house is quieter
quietly worrying that his back won't last until state pension age in a job on his feet
going back into church alone after his dad's funeral and finding it helped more than he expected
card.webcam_photo: Taken in the evening at the kitchen table on an older laptop, with the camera slightly below his eye line so it looks a little up at him. Lighting is the overhead kitchen spotlights, giving a bit of shine on his forehead and a faint shadow under his chin. He's a broad-faced white man in his mid-forties with ruddy cheeks, a short greying beard and close-cropped brown hair thinning at the crown. He's smiling openly and his eyes are crinkled. No glasses. He's wearing a navy fleece over the collar of a work polo shirt. Behind him are white gloss kitchen units with a kettle, a toaster and a stack of post by the bread bin, a fridge covered in magnets and a calendar, and a small window with a roller blind half down. The edge of a dog bed is just visible on the floor at the right of the frame.
